task: T03 of the SmartTube AI-subtitle plan: build an immutable native subtitle timeline for background prefetch. Judge each claim/evidence pair for the snapshot reader and timeline builder before the scheduler and UI work that depends on them.

checks.claim: Decoding the whole file in one input buffer with timeUs = 0 and subsampleOffsetUs = format.subsampleOffsetUs gives event times on the media timeline, and no offset is applied twice.
The reader must poll with a deadline instead of stopping at the first null dequeueOutputBuffer, because this checkout decodes on a background thread.

checks.source: measured decoder output (SubtitleDecoderProbeTest, temporary, deleted after the probe); exoplayer .../text/TextRenderer.java:179-216
checks.claim: One display frame per distinct event time is required because the VTT decoder reports several events at the same microsecond, and treating them as separate frames both creates zero-length frames and double-applies the incremental text rule.
checks.evidence:
Probe output for 'WEBVTT 0-2s Hello, 2-4s World':
  buffer timeUs=0 eos=false events=4 @0=[Hello] @2000000=[World] @2000000=[World] @4000000=
TextRenderer advances while (subtitleNextEventTimeUs <= positionUs) { nextSubtitleEventIndex++; } and then calls getCues(positionUs), so playback shows one content change per instant.
Before collapsing, OriginalSubtitleNormalizer consumed the duplicated [World] event and stripped the repeated text, so the snapshot frame showed an empty string while playback showed 'World'.

checks.source: common/.../SubtitleTimelineBuilder.java (frames are built for every event, including an event with no cues); common/.../OriginalSubtitleNormalizer.java
checks.claim: An event whose cue list is empty is a real clearing boundary and must be kept as an empty frame, while a cue whose text is empty is a text frame.
checks.evidence:
Builder: for each event it creates a SubtitleFrame even when the cue list is empty; SubtitleFrame.isEmpty() reports items.isEmpty().
Reader test asserts: event(1_000_000) with no cues yields timeline.frameAt(1_000_000).isEmpty() == true, while a one-cue event with text "" yields one item with empty text.
OriginalSubtitleNormalizer.normalize(<no cues>) returns an empty list without touching its buffer.

checks.claim: The subtitle MIME type taken from the source metadata selects a decoder that can parse the payload the player will actually download.
checks.evidence:
DEFAULT.createDecoder maps application/x-mp4-vtt to Mp4WebvttDecoder, whose parser reads MP4 boxes (TYPE_vttc) instead of raw text.
CaptionTrack.getMimeType() returns sFormat.mimeType, i.e. whatever the YouTube response declares.
No payload from a real source has been captured in this workspace, so it is unknown whether a YouTube timedtext response declared as application/x-mp4-vtt is really MP4-boxed or plain WEBVTT text.
